evals.prompt: We use Lucide throughout the app but there's no icon for the three things our product actually does. I need 'batch-run', 'data-lineage' and 'rollback-snapshot'. They need to sit in the sidebar next to the Lucide ones and not look bolted on. Icons live in src/icons/ where we've vendored the Lucide SVGs we use.
evals.expected_output: Three new SVGs using Lucide's 24 grid, stroke-width 2, round caps and joins, currentColor, and root-level attributes. They reuse shapes from the vendored set and validate against the combined directory.
expectations: Runs scripts/infer_spec.py against the existing directory before drawing anything
Matches Lucide's conventions exactly: 24 viewBox, stroke-width 2, round linecap and linejoin, currentColor, attributes on the root svg
Reads the existing neighbouring icons rather than drawing from the concept alone
Reuses an arrowhead, container, or similar recurring shape from the extracted registry verbatim
Keeps interior detail sparse, accounting for the heavy 2px stroke on a 24 grid
Runs scripts/validate_icons.py over the combined directory, not only the new files
Leaves pre-existing findings in the vendored Lucide files unchanged
Reports which conventions were matched and any ambiguity that was resolved by guessing

evals.prompt: I need to add about 5 icons to our in-house set. Fair warning, it's a bit of a mess. It was built by two different people and I think they disagreed about some things. Set is at design/icons/. New ones I need: export-csv, archive, restore, merge, split.
evals.expected_output: An inference pass that surfaces the internal inconsistency and records which variant wins. Genuine ambiguity is checked with the user. Five icons are then drawn to that decision and validated.
expectations: Surfaces the set's internal disagreement from infer_spec.py output rather than silently taking the majority
Asks the user which variant to match, or checks which icons are newest, when the split is close
Distinguishes quirks to match from defects not to reproduce, and says which is which
Draws all five icons, not a subset
Reuses extracted registry parts where the set already has them
Validates the new icons against the whole combined set
Applies the stranger test by reviewing the full set as a grid and recording each new icon's neighbor comparison
Leaves the pre-existing inconsistency across old icons outside this task

evals.prompt: can you draw me a 'workflow' icon that matches the rest of our icons? they're phosphor icons, regular weight, in public/icons/
evals.expected_output: Recognition that Phosphor regular is a filled outline on a 256 viewBox with no stroke-width attribute, a heads-up to the user that this is harder than extending a stroked set, and one icon drawn as a closed filled path at the correct weight.
expectations: Identifies that Phosphor uses a 256 viewBox rather than 24
Recognises that Phosphor regular weight is drawn as filled paths, not strokes, so there is no stroke-width to set
Tells the user this is more involved than extending a stroked set before drawing
Produces the icon with fill=currentColor and no stroke attributes
Draws the outline weight at a thickness consistent with Phosphor regular on the 256 grid
Reads existing Phosphor files in the directory to match construction rather than working from the published convention alone
